page: Amazon Web Services c8g.16xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by an ARM64-based AWS Neoverse-V2 processor. The instance features 64 dedicated physical cores running at 2.8 GHz with a 1:1 thread-to-core ratio, meaning hyperthreading is disabled. It is equipped with 128 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core, along with 36 MB of L3 cache. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, the server includes a 30 Gbps baseline network bandwidth but does not bundle local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

In benchmark evaluations, the c8g.16xlarge demonstrates strong multi-threaded capabilities and memory throughput. It achieves a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 109,145.77 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 25,571.0. Its memory subsystem delivers top-tier performance, with read-only bandwidth reaching 7,394.89 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 459.06 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Additionally, the instance performs highly in database operations, scoring 46,812.99 on PassMark and executing 131.06 million Redis SET operations per second.

The dedicated ARM64 architecture provides high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for highly parallelized workloads. However, the lack of local NVMe storage and GPU accelerators represents a tradeoff for storage-intensive or deep learning training tasks. This server is optimally configured for multi-threaded software compilation, high-throughput static web serving, database operations, and medium-scale language model inference.
